string.name: app_name
string.translation_description: The application name, shown under the launcher icon and in the app switcher.

string.name: splash_version
string.translation_description: Version line under the app name on the launch splash. %1$s is the app version name, e.g. 1.2.3

string.name: splash_dismiss
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the action that dismisses the launch splash when it is tapped

string.name: north_pole
string.translation_description: Short abbreviation for the North Celestial Pole, displayed as a label on the sky map grid. Translators: use the standard abbreviation in your language (e.g. NP in English, PN in French).

string.name: south_pole
string.translation_description: Short abbreviation for the South Celestial Pole, displayed as a label on the sky map grid. Translators: use the standard abbreviation in your language (e.g. SP in English, PS in French).

string.name: zenith
string.translation_description: Label for the zenith point (directly overhead) shown on the sky map. Displayed in capitals.

string.name: nadir
string.translation_description: Label for the nadir point (directly below) shown on the sky map. Displayed in capitals.

string.name: north
string.translation_description: Compass direction label shown on the horizon of the sky map. Displayed in capitals.

string.name: south
string.translation_description: Compass direction label shown on the horizon of the sky map. Displayed in capitals.

string.name: east
string.translation_description: Compass direction label shown on the horizon of the sky map. Displayed in capitals.

string.name: west
string.translation_description: Compass direction label shown on the horizon of the sky map. Displayed in capitals.

string.name: ecliptic
string.translation_description: Label for the ecliptic line — the apparent annual path of the Sun across the sky.

string.name: sun
string.translation_description: Name of the Sun, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: moon
string.translation_description: Name of Earth\'s Moon, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: mercury
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Mercury, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: venus
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Venus, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: earth
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Earth.

string.name: mars
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Mars, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: jupiter
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Jupiter, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: saturn
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Saturn, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: uranus
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Uranus, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: neptune
string.translation_description: Name of the planet Neptune, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: pluto
string.translation_description: Name of the dwarf planet Pluto, drawn as a label on the sky map.

string.name: search_button
string.translation_description: Button on the map screen that opens the sky search dialog.

string.name: search_label
string.translation_description: Title of the sky search dialog.

string.name: search_hint
string.translation_description: Placeholder text in the search field showing example search targets.

string.name: search_coordinates_hint
string.translation_description: Helper text under the search field showing that celestial coordinates (right ascension and declination) can be typed directly, with two example formats.

string.name: search_go
string.translation_description: Button that starts navigating the sky map toward the typed search target.

string.name: search_cancel
string.translation_description: Button that dismisses the search dialog or ends the current search.

string.name: search_no_results
string.translation_description: Message shown when a sky search returns no results, suggesting the object may not currently be visible.

resources.string: No results were found. Perhaps the object is not visible at this time.

string.name: search_target_looking_message
string.translation_description: Status shown while the user is being guided toward a search target. %1$s is the object name.

string.name: search_target_found_message
string.translation_description: Status shown when the search target has been found and is centered on screen. %1$s is the object name.

string.name: search_overlay_prompt
string.translation_description: Instruction telling the user to physically point their phone in the direction of the on-screen arrow to find the search target.

resources.string: Point your phone toward the arrow

string.name: layer_stars
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing stars.

string.name: layer_constellations
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing constellation figures and names.

string.name: layer_deep_sky
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing deep-sky objects such as galaxies and nebulae.

string.name: layer_solar_system
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing the Sun, Moon, and planets.

string.name: layer_meteor_showers
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing the radiant points of annual meteor showers.

string.name: layer_satellites
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing artificial satellites such as the International Space Station.

string.name: channel_passes_name
string.translation_description: Name of the notification channel for alerts shortly before a satellite passes overhead.

string.name: channel_passes_description
string.translation_description: Description of the satellite-pass notification channel.

resources.string: A single alert shortly before the best visible pass of the night

string.name: notif_pass_title
string.translation_description: Title of the notification sent shortly before a satellite passes overhead. %1$s is the satellite name.

string.name: notif_pass_text
string.translation_description: Body of the satellite pass notification, telling the user when to go outside. %1$s is a time.

resources.string: Visible from about %1$s — head outside and let your eyes adjust

string.name: channel_eclipses_name
string.translation_description: Name of the notification channel for alerts before a lunar eclipse starts.

string.name: channel_eclipses_description
string.translation_description: Description of the lunar-eclipse notification channel.

resources.string: A single alert before a lunar eclipse begins

string.name: notif_eclipse_title
string.translation_description: Title of the notification sent before a lunar eclipse starts. %1$s is a localized eclipse type like \'Total lunar eclipse\'.

string.name: notif_eclipse_text
string.translation_description: Body of the lunar eclipse notification, telling the user when it begins. %1$s is a time.

resources.string: Begins around %1$s — worth stepping outside for

string.name: satellite_name_iss
string.translation_description: Display name for the International Space Station.

string.name: satellite_name_tiangong
string.translation_description: Display name for the Chinese space station Tiangong.

string.name: layer_param_pass_alerts
string.translation_description: Label for the setting that turns on a notification shortly before a satellite passes overhead.

string.name: layer_param_pass_alerts_description
string.translation_description: Explains what the pass-alert setting does: a single notification before the best visible pass of the night.

resources.string: Notify me before the best visible pass each night

string.name: layer_param_eclipse_alerts
string.translation_description: Label for the setting that turns on a notification before a lunar eclipse begins.

string.name: layer_param_eclipse_alerts_description
string.translation_description: Explains what the eclipse-alert setting does: a single notification before a lunar eclipse starts.

resources.string: Notify me before a lunar eclipse starts

string.name: satellite_description
string.translation_description: Short description shown on the info card for an artificial satellite.

resources.string: An artificial satellite in low Earth orbit, sunlit against a dark sky. It crosses from horizon to horizon in a few minutes, moving steadily and without blinking.

string.name: satellite_next_pass
string.translation_description: Heading above the next visible pass details on a satellite\'s info card.

string.name: satellite_pass_when
string.translation_description: When and how high the next satellite pass will be. %1$s is a time, %2$s is a compass direction, %3$d is an angle in degrees.

string.name: satellite_pass_magnitude
string.translation_description: How bright the satellite will be at its peak. %1$.1f is a brightness magnitude.

string.name: satellite_pass_shadow
string.translation_description: Tells the user the satellite will fade out mid-pass when it enters the Earth\'s shadow. %1$s is a time.

string.name: satellite_no_pass
string.translation_description: Shown on a satellite info card when no visible pass is coming up in the next two days.

resources.string: No visible passes in the next couple of days

string.name: satellite_pass_unknown
string.translation_description: Shown on a satellite info card when the downloaded orbit data is too old to predict pass times reliably.

resources.string: Orbit data is too old to predict passes

string.name: object_info_eclipse_title
string.translation_description: Heading above the next lunar eclipse details on the Moon\'s info card.

string.name: object_info_no_eclipse
string.translation_description: Shown on the Moon\'s info card when no lunar eclipse is coming up in the searched time range.

string.name: object_info_eclipse_greatest
string.translation_description: The next lunar eclipse\'s type and greatest-eclipse date/time. %1$s is a localized eclipse type like \'Total lunar eclipse\', %2$s a date, %3$s a time.

string.name: object_info_eclipse_totality
string.translation_description: The start and end time of totality during a total lunar eclipse. %1$s and %2$s are times.

string.name: tonight_satellite_pass
string.translation_description: Tonight-widget row announcing a visible satellite pass. %1$s is the satellite name, %2$s is a time of day.

string.name: tonight_trailing_pass
string.translation_description: Small trailing note on a satellite pass row. %1$s is a compass direction, %2$d is an angle in degrees, %3$.1f is a brightness magnitude.

string.name: satellites_no_data
string.translation_description: Explanation shown when satellite orbital data has not been downloaded yet and so no satellites can be drawn.

resources.string: Satellite positions need an internet connection to update.

string.name: satellites_refresh
string.translation_description: Button that tries to download satellite orbital data now.

string.name: satellites_retry_soon
string.translation_description: Shown instead of a Refresh button when satellite data was just requested and cannot be requested again for a few minutes.

resources.string: Try again in a few minutes

string.name: satellites_retry_within_hour
string.translation_description: Shown instead of a Refresh button when satellite data cannot be requested again for up to an hour.

string.name: satellites_retry_hours
string.translation_description: Shown instead of a Refresh button when satellite data cannot be requested again for several hours.

resources.string: Try again in a few hours

string.name: satellites_retry_tomorrow
string.translation_description: Shown instead of a Refresh button when satellite data cannot be requested again until the next day.

string.name: satellites_retry_days
string.translation_description: Shown instead of a Refresh button when satellite data cannot be requested again for several days.

resources.string: Try again in a few days

string.name: layer_grid
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing the right ascension / declination grid.

string.name: layer_horizon
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing the horizon line and compass points.

string.name: layer_ecliptic
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the layer showing the ecliptic line.

string.name: layer_sky_gradient
string.translation_description: Toggle label for the daytime sky-brightness gradient drawn behind the sky map.

string.name: layers_sheet_title
string.translation_description: Title of the bottom sheet listing sky map layers the user can show or hide.

string.name: layers_group_objects
string.translation_description: Layers-sheet group header for layers that draw sky objects (stars, planets, deep-sky objects).

string.name: layers_group_reference
string.translation_description: Layers-sheet group header for reference elements drawn over the sky (coordinate grid, horizon, ecliptic).

string.name: layers_group_display
string.translation_description: Layers-sheet group header for display settings that change how the sky is rendered rather than what is drawn.

string.name: show_layers
string.translation_description: Accessibility description and label for the button opening the layer-visibility sheet, which holds the layers that do not fit on the rail plus display options.

string.name: more_button
string.translation_description: Accessibility label and tooltip for the map-screen button (three vertical dots) opening the overflow menu of further destinations such as Gallery and Settings.

string.name: night_mode
string.translation_description: Label for the toggle switching the display to a dim red night-vision-preserving mode.

string.name: switch_to_manual
string.translation_description: Tooltip and accessibility label for the button that switches the map from auto (sensor-driven) mode to manual (drag) mode.

string.name: switch_to_auto
string.translation_description: Tooltip and accessibility label for the button that switches the map from manual (drag) mode to auto (sensor-driven) mode.

string.name: no_sensor_warning
string.translation_description: Warning shown when the device lacks the motion sensors needed to point the map at the sky automatically.

resources.string: This device has no compass or motion sensors, so Sky Map can\'t follow where you point it. Drag the map by hand instead.

string.name: no_sensor_warning_dismiss
string.translation_description: Button that dismisses the missing-sensors warning dialog.

string.name: hud_ra_label
string.translation_description: Map-HUD row label: right ascension of the point at the centre of the screen. Standard astronomy abbreviation; keep short.

string.name: hud_dec_label
string.translation_description: Map-HUD row label: declination of the point at the centre of the screen. Standard astronomy abbreviation; keep short.

string.name: hud_alt_label
string.translation_description: Map-HUD row label: altitude (angle above the horizon) of the point at the centre of the screen. Keep short.

string.name: hud_az_label
string.translation_description: Map-HUD row label: azimuth (compass bearing) of the point at the centre of the screen. Keep short.

string.name: hud_fov_label
string.translation_description: Map-HUD row label: the field of view (how many degrees of sky the screen spans). Keep short.

string.name: hud_correction_label
string.translation_description: Map-HUD row label for the manual sensor-alignment correction the user set by dragging. Keep very short.

string.name: hud_ra_value
string.translation_description: Right ascension in the conventional hours-and-minutes notation, e.g. \'18h 38m\'. %1$d is hours (0-23), %2$02d is minutes (00-59).

string.name: hud_signed_degrees_value
string.translation_description: An angle in degrees with an explicit sign and one decimal, e.g. \'+38.8°\'. %1$+.1f is the angle.

string.name: hud_azimuth_value
string.translation_description: A compass bearing with its cardinal-direction abbreviation, e.g. \'312° NW\'. %1$d is whole degrees (0-359), %2$s is the abbreviation.

string.name: hud_fov_value
string.translation_description: Field of view in whole degrees, e.g. \'45°\'. %1$d is the number of degrees.

string.name: hud_fov_value_fine
string.translation_description: Field of view between one and ten degrees, with one decimal, e.g. \'5.5°\'. %1$.1f is the number of degrees.

string.name: hud_fov_value_finest
string.translation_description: Field of view under one degree, with two decimals, e.g. \'0.25°\'. %1$.2f is the number of degrees.

string.name: hud_correction_value
string.translation_description: The sensor-alignment correction pair: azimuth then altitude offset, each signed with one decimal, e.g. \'+4.5° −1.2°\'.

string.name: hud_correction_reset
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the small button that clears the manual sensor-alignment correction back to zero.

string.name: hud_alignment_reset_message
string.translation_description: Snackbar confirming the sensor-alignment correction was cleared; shown with an Undo action.

string.name: hud_fov_locked
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the small lock icon shown next to the field-of-view readout while the camera controls the zoom in through-camera mode.

string.name: layer_hud
string.translation_description: Layers-sheet Display toggle that shows the heads-up readout of where the phone is pointing (compass direction and altitude) over the star map.

string.name: layer_camera
string.translation_description: Layers-sheet Display toggle that shows the live rear-camera image behind the star map, so the drawn sky overlays the real one.

string.name: layer_camera_needs_sensors
string.translation_description: Subtitle explaining why the through-camera toggle is disabled: the device has no usable motion sensors, and the mode needs the map to follow where the phone points.

resources.string: Needs motion sensors this device doesn\'t have

string.name: ar_auto_mode_snackbar
string.translation_description: Snackbar shown when turning on through-camera mode switched the map from manual dragging back to automatic sensor pointing.

resources.string: Auto mode turned on for the camera view

string.name: ar_permission_denied
string.translation_description: Snackbar shown when the user declined the camera permission that through-camera mode needs.

resources.string: Through-camera mode needs the camera permission

string.name: ar_permission_settings_action
string.translation_description: Snackbar action opening the app\'s system settings page so the user can grant the camera permission after permanently denying it.

string.name: ar_exposure_slider
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the slider adjusting the camera\'s exposure compensation while through-camera mode is on.

string.name: ar_alignment_adjusted_message
string.translation_description: Snackbar shown after the user drags the star map to align it with the camera image; shown with an Undo action that reverts the whole drag.

string.name: ar_dimmer_slider
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the slider dimming the camera image behind the star map while through-camera mode is on.

string.name: ar_iso_slider_label
string.translation_description: Very short label for the temporary developer slider setting the camera\'s manual ISO sensitivity in through-camera mode. Standard photography abbreviation; keep as-is.

string.name: ar_iso_slider
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the temporary developer slider setting the camera\'s manual ISO sensitivity in through-camera mode.

string.name: ar_shutter_slider_label
string.translation_description: Very short label for the temporary developer slider setting the camera\'s manual shutter (exposure) time in through-camera mode.

string.name: ar_shutter_slider
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the temporary developer slider setting the camera\'s manual shutter (exposure) time in through-camera mode.

string.name: share_button
string.translation_description: Overflow-menu row that captures the current sky view as an image and opens the system share sheet.

string.name: share_chooser_title
string.translation_description: Title of the system share sheet when sharing a captured sky image.

string.name: share_invitation
string.translation_description: Short invitation stamped on the footer of shared sky images, above the store link.

resources.string: See what you\'re looking at — get Sky Map free

string.name: share_text
string.translation_description: Text accompanying a shared sky image in apps that accept both an image and text. %1$s is the app-store link.

resources.string: See what you\'re looking at — get Sky Map free: %1$s

string.name: share_layout_overlay
string.translation_description: Caption of the share-layout choice that draws the star map over the camera photo, as seen on screen.

string.name: share_layout_side_by_side
string.translation_description: Caption of the share-layout choice that puts the camera photo and the star map next to each other.

string.name: share_shutter_button
string.translation_description: Accessibility label for the round shutter button that captures and shares the current through-camera view.

string.name: share_failed_message
string.translation_description: Snackbar shown when capturing the sky image for sharing failed.

resources.string: Couldn\'t capture the sky — try again

string.name: ar_exposure_auto
string.translation_description: Readout shown when a manual camera exposure slider sits at its automatic position.

string-array.name: hud_cardinal_directions
string-array.translation_description: The sixteen compass-point abbreviations, clockwise from north, used as the azimuth suffix in the map HUD (e.g. N, NNE, NE...). Translate to the locale\'s conventional compass abbreviations.

string.name: time_travel_button
string.translation_description: Label for the button opening the time travel dialog, which shows the sky at another date.

string.name: time_travel_title
string.translation_description: Title of the time travel dialog.

string.name: time_travel_visiting
string.translation_description: Readout in the time travel dialog showing the currently chosen destination date and time. %1$s is the formatted date and time.

string.name: time_travel_pick_date
string.translation_description: Button in the time travel dialog that opens a date picker.

string.name: time_travel_pick_time
string.translation_description: Button in the time travel dialog that opens a time picker.

string.name: time_travel_select_event
string.translation_description: Placeholder hint for the dropdown list of popular astronomical events in the time travel dialog.

string.name: time_travel_go
string.translation_description: Button that starts time travel to the chosen date.

string.name: time_travel_from_now
string.translation_description: Button that starts time travel from the present moment, letting the user play time forward or backward from now.

string.name: time_travel_ok
string.translation_description: Confirmation button in the date and time pickers.

string.name: time_travel_cancel
string.translation_description: Button that closes a time travel dialog without doing anything.

string.name: time_travel_slower
string.translation_description: Player button that steps the time travel playback rate one step backward (slower forward, or faster backward). Rendered as a double left-pointing symbol.

string.name: time_travel_pause
string.translation_description: Player button that freezes time travel playback. Rendered as a pause symbol.

string.name: time_travel_faster
string.translation_description: Player button that steps the time travel playback rate one step forward (faster forward, or slower backward). Rendered as a double right-pointing symbol.

string.name: time_travel_return
string.translation_description: Player button that ends time travel and returns the map to the present.

string.name: time_travel_second_speed
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means forward.

string.name: time_travel_minute_speed
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means forward.

string.name: time_travel_10minute_speed
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means forward.

string.name: time_travel_hour_speed
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means forward.

string.name: time_travel_day_speed
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means forward.

string.name: time_travel_week_speed
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means forward.

string.name: time_travel_second_speed_back
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means backward.

string.name: time_travel_minute_speed_back
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means backward.

string.name: time_travel_10minute_speed_back
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means backward.

string.name: time_travel_hour_speed_back
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means backward.

string.name: time_travel_day_speed_back
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means backward.

string.name: time_travel_week_speed_back
string.translation_description: Label showing rate of travel through time. The symbol means backward.

string.name: time_travel_now
string.translation_description: Time travel picker entry that resets the destination to the present moment.

string.name: time_travel_next_sunset
string.translation_description: Name of a popular astronomical event in the time travel picker.

string.name: time_travel_next_sunrise
string.translation_description: Name of a popular astronomical event in the time travel picker.

string.name: time_travel_next_full_moon
string.translation_description: Name of a popular astronomical event in the time travel picker.

string.name: time_travel_next_new_moon
string.translation_description: Name of a popular astronomical event in the time travel picker.

string.name: time_travel_six_planet_parade_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A planet parade is when several planets are visible at once. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_lunar_eclipse_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_lyrids_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. The Lyrids are an annual meteor shower. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_venus_jupiter_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A conjunction is when two planets appear very close together in the sky. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_mars_uranus_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A close approach is when two objects appear near each other in the sky. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_solar_eclipse_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_perseids_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. The Perseids are an annual meteor shower. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_lunar_eclipse_aug_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_jupiter_occultation_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A lunar occultation is when the Moon passes in front of a planet, briefly hiding it. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_geminids_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. The Geminids are an annual meteor shower. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_supermoon_2026
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A supermoon is a full moon that occurs near the Moon\'s closest approach to Earth. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_mercury_transit_2016
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A Mercury transit is when Mercury passes across the face of the Sun as seen from Earth. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

string.name: time_travel_solar_eclipse_2024
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. Keep the date format suitable for your locale.

resources.string: North American Solar Eclipse of Apr 8, 2024

string.name: time_travel_apollo_11
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker: the first crewed Moon landing in 1969.

string.name: time_travel_jupiter_saturn_2020
string.translation_description: Name of an astronomical event in the time travel picker. A conjunction is when two planets appear very close together in the sky.

string.name: sun_wont_set_message
string.translation_description: Message shown when the sun will not set (or rise) during the next 24 hours at the user\'s location (polar day or polar night).

resources.string: The sun will not set during the next 24 hours at your current location.

string.name: time_travel_start_message
string.translation_description: Toast message when time travel starts toward a chosen destination. %1$s is the formatted destination date and time.

string.name: time_travel_close_message
string.translation_description: Toast message shown when the user exits time travel and returns to the present.

string.name: location_management_title
string.translation_description: Title of the location management sheet

string.name: location_source_auto
string.translation_description: Label shown when the device is determining location automatically

string.name: location_source_manual
string.translation_description: Label shown when the user has manually entered their location

string.name: location_source_acquiring
string.translation_description: Label shown while waiting for the first automatic location fix

string.name: location_source_unset
string.translation_description: Label shown when no location has been set

string.name: location_source_hardware_unavailable
string.translation_description: Label shown when the device has no location hardware

string.name: location_switch_to_auto
string.translation_description: Button to switch from manual location to automatic detection

string.name: location_switch_to_manual
string.translation_description: Button to switch from automatic to manual location entry

string.name: location_change
string.translation_description: Button to change or update the manually entered location

string.name: location_set_toast
string.translation_description: Toast message when a location is acquired or entered. %1$s is the place name or coordinates

string.name: location_long_lat
string.translation_description: Formatted display of longitude and latitude. %1$.2f is longitude, %2$.2f is latitude

string.name: location_map_unavailable
string.translation_description: Message shown in the map area of the location sheet when the static map image cannot be loaded

string.name: location_map_content_description

string.translation_description: Information for the user on how to calibrate the compass when the screen auto-opens. Placeholder is the video URL. Please do not change the < and > markup - the <blockquote> renders as a highlighted callout

resources.string:
Your phone\'s compass sensor is reporting poor calibration. The figure-8 motion (watch a demonstration) prompts your phone\'s hardware to reset its compass sensor — Sky Map has no control over this process.

Calibrated does not mean accurate. The figure-8 gesture helps reset the sensor, but it cannot remove interference from nearby metal objects, car dashboards, or phone cases. If the map is still off after calibrating, those external sources are the most likely cause — not Sky Map.
Move to an open area away from metal and try again.

string.name: calibration_what_to_do_user
string.translation_description: Information for the user on how to calibrate the compass when they open the calibration screen. Placeholder is the video URL. Please do not change the < and > markup - the <blockquote> renders as a highlighted callout

resources.string:
Your phone is reporting its compass calibration status as shown above.

If necessary, perform the figure-8 motion (watch a demonstration) to prompt your phone\'s hardware to recalibrate its compass sensor.

Important: calibration helps the sensor reset itself internally. It does not mean the compass is necessarily accurate! Local magnetic interference (metal objects, car dashboards, phone cases) can still cause your phone\'s compass to send inaccurate readings to Sky Map.
If the map isn\'t showing positions correctly the problem is likely your phone - not Sky Map!
